Subject: Phased adoption checkpoints & pricing review for Nimbus Analytics

Hi Emily / Mark,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — appreciate you walking us through the latency and throughput expectations for your analytics workloads. Based on our conversation I sketched a phased adoption plan (attached) that ties evaluation gates to specific commercial milestones so both teams have a clear path to production and renewal triggers. High level: 

- Phase A (Pilot, 4 weeks): small-scale eval (up to 5k tokens/day) — goal: validate latency and embedding quality.
- Phase B (Ramp, 8–12 weeks): increased load (target 50k tokens/day) with autoscaling and prefix caching enabled.
- Phase C (Production): sustained throughput with SLA and uplift to committed pricing.

Commercial mechanics I propose in the attachment: an initial evaluation credit, a one-time ramp discount that phases out when the 50k tokens/day threshold sustains for 14 consecutive days, and a renewal uplift clause that converts usage ramp into a higher committed tier at renewal.

Please find a draft Mutual Action Plan attached (Nimbus_MAP_v1.pdf). If this structure looks right, we can schedule 30 minutes to firm up milestone dates and procurement timing.

Next steps I recommend:
- You confirm the internal stakeholders / procurement timeline.
- We agree on the Pilot start date (we can spin the pilot environment within 48 hours once we have an NDA).
- I’ll prepare a short SOW and a HubSpot deal record for tracking.

Sending Marissa on copy to help with pricing specifics.

Cheers,
Diego

Emily — good questions. Answers inline and updated MAP attached (Nimbus_MAP_v1.1.pdf).

1) Ramp discount: we typically offer a 30% one-time ramp discount applied to usage in Phase B for the first 6 weeks, dropping to 15% for weeks 7–12 if the usage target is met. If the 50k tokens/day threshold is sustained for 14 consecutive days, Phase C pricing (committed tier) activates.

2) Pilot enablement: a PO is acceptable for starting the Pilot under a standard Master Services Addendum (MSA) we provide; however, we require a signed SOW for Dedicated/Committed capacity. For the Pilot we can proceed with a PO + pilot SOW that references the MAP.

3) Price protection: I’ve added a fixed-rate protection clause for the ramp window (Phase A–B) in the MAP — we won’t increase the per-token price during the 12-week ramp other than agreed adjustments in the MAP.

Attached are: updated MAP and a short SOW stub for pilot activities. Also creating the HubSpot deal now (will include the deal link in follow-up).

Propose a 30-minute call tomorrow 11am PT to lock milestone dates.

Thanks,
Diego

Diego — quick internal note for the thread, copied externally for transparency. Pricing team is comfortable with the structure but recommends we codify two things in writing: 

- A clearly defined usage gate (we propose: 50,000 tokens/day sustained for 14 days) that triggers conversion to the committed tier and lifts the ramp discount.
- A one-time ramp credit that is applied as an invoice-level discount (we recommend a $15k credit applied during Phase B, prorated weekly if they don’t hit the sustained threshold).

If Nimbus values predictability we can offer an additional renewal incentive: a 6-month renewal rate guarantee if they agree to a 12-month commit after the ramp. That becomes our uplift lever in the MAP.

Suggest we include these as discrete line items in the SOW and in the HubSpot milestone checklist.

—Marissa
